title: Paper 1 Unit 1 & 2 Teaching & Research Aptitude Sprint Test

questions.question_text: Which of the following levels of teaching involves the highest level of cognitive interaction, where learners actively formulate hypotheses and solve unstructured problems?
questions.explanation: Hunt's Reflective Level represents the highest cognitive stratum in teaching hierarchy. At this level, students engage in deep inquiry, critical evaluation, problem solving, and reflective thinking beyond rote recall (Memory level) and conceptual relationships (Understanding level).
questions.numerical_formula: Cognitive Hierarchy: Memory Level (Herbart) < Understanding Level (Morrison) < Reflective Level (Hunt).
questions.common_pitfalls: Students frequently confuse Morrison's Understanding level with Hunt's Reflective level.

questions.question_text: In experimental research, when an unobserved external variable concurrently influences both the independent variable and the dependent variable, causing a spurious association, it is called a:
questions.explanation: A confounding variable is an outside influence that changes the effect of a dependent and independent variable. This risk is resolved via randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or ANCOVA statistical controls.
questions.numerical_formula: Spurious Correlation: r_xy driven by hidden z => Partial correlation r_{xy.z} = (r_{xy} - r_{xz}r_{yz}) / (sqrt(1-r_{xz}^2)*sqrt(1-r_{yz}^2)).
questions.common_pitfalls: Confusing intervening variables (which mediate the path X -> M -> Y) with confounding variables (which cause both X and Y).
